{{Short description|Pennsylvania-based opinion poll}}
{{Use American English|date=May 2026}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=May 2026}}
The '''Franklin & Marshall College Poll''' (formerly the '''Keystone Poll''') is a Pennsylvania-based [[opinion poll]].<ref>"[https://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/tag/franklin-and-marshall-college-poll/ Franklin and Marshall College Poll]." Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: CBS Philly, retrieved online June 2019.</ref><ref>Brennan, Chris. "[https://www.inquirer.com/philly/news/politics/presidential/At-the-FM-Poll-a-review-of-2016-to-sharpen-future-surveys.html At the F&M poll, a review of 2016 to sharpen future surveys]." Philadelphia, Pennsylvania: ''The Inquirer'', February 27, 2017.</ref><ref name="about">{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |year=2016 |title=About the Franklin & Marshall College Poll |url=http://www.fandm.edu/politics/the-franklin-marshall-college-poll |access-date= |work= |publisher=Center for Opinion Research, Franklin & Marshall College}}</ref> The poll tracks citizen opinion on politics, public affairs, public policy, and elections in Pennsylvania. 

==History==
The [[Franklin & Marshall College]] Poll first developed from a poll taken during the [[United States Senate special election in Pennsylvania, 1991]], pitting incumbent Democrat [[Harris Wofford]] against former Pennsylvania governor [[Dick Thornburgh]].<ref name=about /> In 1992, the poll was formally inaugurated as the Keystone Poll at [[Millersville University of Pennsylvania]], with [[Terry Madonna]] working as the director of the poll and Berwood Yost, as the head methodologist.<ref name=about /> Yost and Madonna took positions at [[Franklin & Marshall College]] in [[Lancaster, Pennsylvania]], in 2003, bringing the poll with them.<ref name=about /> The poll underwent two significant changes in 2008: it was renamed the Franklin & Marshall College Poll and it was expanded beyond its Pennsylvania roots to study national opinion for 29 [[Hearst-Argyle]] televisions stations and other media outlets.<ref name=about /> 

During its existence, the poll has been published through a variety of media outlets.<ref>"Franklin and Marshall College Poll," CBS Philly.</ref><ref name=about /> In its early years, it was carried by the ''[[Philadelphia Daily News]]'' and [[KYW-TV]].<ref name=about /> Later, the [[WTXF-TV|Fox 29]] replaced KYW and the ''[[Harrisburg Patriot News]]'' and the ''[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]'' began carrying the poll.<ref name=about /> In 2002, the [[Comcast Network]] replaced [[WTXF-TV|Fox 29]]. The statewide distribution now includes [[WPVI-TV]], [[WGAL-TV]],<ref>"[https://www.wgal.com/article/news-8-franklin-and-marshall-college-poll-released/5732464 News 8 Franklin and Marshall College poll released]." Lancaster, Pennsylvania: WGAL-TV, September 26, 2012.</ref> [[WTAE-TV]], and the [[Times-Shamrock Communications]].<ref name=about />

The Center for Opinion Research at Franklin & Marshall College conducts the F&M Poll. As a department of the college, the Center is both non-profit and non-partisan. The Center is directed by Berwood Yost, who also now directs the F&M Poll, since Terry Madonna has retired. Mr. Yost also works closely with Stephen Medvic, the Honorable and Mrs. John C. Kunkel Professor of Government at F&M, who is the director of F&M’s Center for Politics and Public Affairs.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
